title: Sloppy Joes
subtitle: saucy, sweet-tangy ground beef piled on toasted buns: a 30-minute classic
imageAlt: Two sloppy joe sandwiches on toasted buns overflowing with saucy ground beef, on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: about 8 sandwiches: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Brown sugar, Worcestershire, vinegar, paprika, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: No green pepper in this version: onion, garlic and a tangy-sweet tomato sauce do the work.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Cook the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Spoon off the fat, add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, vinegar, paprika, salt and pepper.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough to mound on a spoon.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet or under the broiler 1–2 minutes, until golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the filling on the bottom buns and cover with the tops.

fixIt.fix: Simmer a few minutes more, uncovered; it should mound, not pour.
Add another ½ tsp vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Drain the fat well after browning; lean beef helps.

saleTip: Ground beef and buns are both weekly No Frills sale items; the filling freezes, so double it when beef is cheap.
swap: Ground turkey: same amount, cooked to 74°C (165°F) with no pink.
leftovers: Spoon over a baked potato, or over rice or macaroni with cheddar.
doneness: Ground beef cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested sloppy joe methods (Canadian Living, Heinz): browned ground beef simmered in tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire and vinegar.
prepAhead: Make the filling up to 3 days ahead and reheat; it thickens, so add a splash of water.
reheat: Covered in a pan over medium-low with a splash of water, stirring, or in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Tomato sauce, ketchup and brown sugar; no Worcestershire or garlic.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the Worcestershire and paprika.

fancy.note: Melted old cheddar on buttered, toasted buns.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: butter the cut sides before toasting.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: top the filling with the cheddar and broil 1 minute to melt before adding the bun tops.

plating: Serve open-faced with a knife and fork.

why.0-7: A spoon of vinegar brightens the sauce so it doesn't taste flat-sweet.
why.0-6: Worcestershire adds deep, savoury flavour without heat.

funFact: Sloppy joes probably started as a 1930s loose-meat sandwich in Sioux City, Iowa, though several diners claim the name.

keeps.note: freeze the filling flat in bags; buns separately
